extracted.intended_audience: members and staff of the Administrative Conference, and researchers preparing or submitting project proposals for ACUS recommendations
extracted.subtask_description: Describes the Administrative Conference's Project Process and procedural steps required to develop, consider, and adopt formal recommendations or statements. Applies to researchers, committees, Council, and Conference membership involved in ACUS projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Process (overall)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Conference’s research and the resulting recommendations are conducted through our Project Process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Project Process is the overarching framework governing how recommendations are developed and adopted; individual steps of the process (gathering/selecting ideas, Council approval, selecting the researcher, committee consideration of the report, committee formulation of a recommendation, Council and full membership consideration, and implementation activities) are components of this overall process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gathering and selecting ideas for a project
rubrics_metrics.description: Gathering and selecting ideas for a project is an explicit initial step of the Project Process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project topics must first be proposed and selected as part of the Project Process before further action (researcher selection, study, and recommendation formulation) proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Getting Council approval is a required step in the Project Process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A project cannot proceed to researcher selection and substantive work without approval from the Conference Council; Council consideration is an explicit gate in the workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting the researcher
rubrics_metrics.description: Selecting the researcher is a distinct step in the Project Process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After Council approval, the Conference selects a researcher to carry out the study that will inform committee consideration and recommendation drafting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Researcher's report considered by a committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Having the researcher’s report considered by a committee is part of the process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The researcher's report serves as the basis for committee review and deliberation; committee consideration is required before a formal recommendation is formulated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee formulates a recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: The selected committee formulates a recommendation based on the researcher’s report and committee deliberations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A committee synthesizes findings and drafts the formal recommendation that will be submitted to the Council and full Conference membership for further consideration and possible adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council and full Conference membership consideration
rubrics_metrics.description: A committee’s recommendation is considered by the Council and then the full Conference membership.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations undergo sequential review: committee → Council → full Conference membership. Both levels of consideration are part of the approval pathway prior to adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption by voting members at semi-annual plenary sessions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations are adopted by the voting members of the Conference at semi-annual plenary sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal adoption occurs at plenary sessions held semi-annually and requires a vote of the Conference's voting members; this is the definitive act that converts a committee recommendation into an official Conference recommendation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation activities after adoption
rubrics_metrics.description: Implementation activities follow adoption of a recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After a recommendation is adopted, the Conference engages in implementation activities to promote or effectuate the recommendation's aims; implementation is an explicit post-adoption phase of the Project Process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements as an alternative product
rubrics_metrics.description: On occasion, the Conference membership has adopted a 'Statement' to express views on a matter without making a formal recommendation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conference statements are typically produced by the same Project Process that leads to recommendations but may set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments rather than recommendations. Historically, from 1968 through 1995 the Conference adopted 17 such statements, and these are included in the searchable database of recommendations.
